about: The two places where the example pack `trampolines` changes OS 1.7.3+0 of the OP-1 Field (docs/first-pack.md). No byte of the firmware is in this file.

It has the form of profiles/op1f-1.7.3.json, which says what each field means. A pack of your own comes with a file like this one: its places under patches, and under tables which function of yours goes to which place.

tools/place_sum.py works out a place's sum from your own firmware file and says how many bytes a trampoline has to copy there. tools/table_build.py writes the pack's table, trampolines_table.s, from this file.
module_base and reserved_bytes are the room for our code, as the main profile names it: the pack is linked for the room behind the loader.

patches.name: The entry of the function that draws a text with the bitmap font. The start-up calls it once, for the version text on the start screen.
The entry of a small function with one argument, which the start-up calls once, right after it has drawn the version text.

entries.does: Counts the call, then goes on into the firmware's function through a trampoline of eight bytes.
Writes one line into the log, then goes on into the firmware's function through a trampoline of twelve bytes.
